notes:
Data corresponding to experiments published in:

Villanueva, R., Paul, M., & Schlurmann, T. (in review). Flexible anchored mats of 
artificial seagrass for restoration: wave dynamics and agreement with contemporary 
models. Scientific Reports

The data correspond to the measurements done on a wave flume for wave interaction with submerged anchored base layers and artificial vegetation. The experiments were done within the framework of the SeaArt project (see the institute's website). The datasets are organized through a specific nomenclature described in the text file Nomenclature.txt.

resources.description:
Data containing all parameters calculated and used in Figures 4,5,6 and 11 in Villanueva et al 2023. 

M0, M1 and M2 contain the same data as DATA, separated by mat configuration

DATA:
Hr -> Wave height ratio to position 1 (leading edge of canopy)
uc -> steady flow component of measured orbital velocity
uw -> wave velocity
rms (suffix) -> root mean square
min -> minimum
max -> maximum
a1M0 (suffix) -> alternative calculation based on value measured for the control experiments (no vegetation) at ADV1
ratio (suffix) -> ratio of max and min (absolute value)
om -> circular frequency omega
A0 -> wave orbital velocity amplitude
A1 (suffix) -> ratio to leading edge value (ADV1) of same measurement
alpha -> flow attenuation parameter. The 2 subsequent digits indicate the positions for the ratio caluclatio. e.g. 13 = ratio between values measured at postions 1 and 3
*_red_* -> velocity reduction in percent [%]. positive indicates velocitiy increase. The 2 subsequent digits indicate the positions for the velocity change. e.g. 13 = ratio between values measured at postions 1 and 3
A_S_ratio -> A0/S where S is the stem separation
l_eff -> effecive length (see Villanueva et al. 2022)
*_r_* -> ratio
m (suffix) -> mean
e (suffix) -> error
KC -> Keulegan-Carpenter Number
Re -> Reynolds Number
Re_bv -> stem-based Re
C_D -> Drag Coefficient
Beta -> damping coefficient
for C_D and Beta, the suffixes are as follows:
	flat -> fixed value 
	C_D_villa -> value calculated by Villanueva et al. 2022
	losa -> value calculated following Losada et al. 2016
	dalr -> following Dalrymple et al. 1984
	Lei -> value after Lei and Nepf 2019b
L -> Wavelength
resources.name: All Calculated Parameters

resources.description:
The datasets here contain the calculated wave decay data (beta in Villanueva et al. 2023, see Figure 3).

Each data set contains tables for all mat configurations and ADV positions such that the different datasets differ in wave condition only. See Nomenclature for naming convention. 

Within each .MAT file the following information can be found:
TABLES:
H_r -> ratio of wave height to incident wave height at position 1. Data at each z-position (ADV height) 
PA -> Phase Average
Hr_m -> ratio of wave height to incident wave height at position 1. Mean and standard deviation of all measurements (z-positions)

STRUCTURES:
PhaseAvg_full -> phase averaged data for each USS and Mat configuration
	NoSample -> number of samples used during for the bins phase averaging

Hr_ASG -> x position (see experimental set-up) and ratios used to fit equation 1 (Villanueva et al, 2023)

Hr_fits -> beta (damp_Coeff) and fit coefficients
resources.name: Wave Decay (Damping Coefficient)

resources.description:
The datasets here contain the calculated velocity structure data (see Figure 7 in Villanueva et al. 2023).

Each data set contains a structure for all mat configurations and ADV positions such that the different datasets differ in wave condition only. See Nomenclature for naming convention. 

Within each .MAT file the following information can be found:
VARIABLES:
d -> depth condition
x -> x-position (see experimental set-up)
WC_m -> wave condition (first value is T and second value is H)

STRUCTURES:
ADV_z -> all preliminary post-processed (first step after raw) data of the ADV at each x and z position

M0,M1,M2 -> data for each mat configuration and ADV showing the phase average, time-synchronous average, wave root mean sqaure velocity, current component
resources.name: Velocity Structure (Orbital Velocities)

resources.description:
In this folder there are several .MAT files with the time series (TS) of A/S and alpha_w for the curves based on Lowe et al. (2005). My curves match those of the authors within the inertia-dominated (left) and general flow areas, but not within the unidirectional flow section, as the curves all kind of converge there. 

The data used for the publication (Figure 10 in Villanueva et al. 2023) comes from A_S_vs_Alpha_lambda. See below for a description of the contents of the .MAT file

I wanted to find out to what parameters the curves were sensitive, therefore, varying the parameters in the suffix of each name here, I created different datasets of TS. 

RESULTS:
Interestingly, the curves are not at all sensitive to the wave period T. The only change observable for longer periods is that the curve started changing values at A/S higher (above 10^0), but then followed almost the same path.

C_D barely made a change, shifting the curve at higher A/S values up or down slightly, but not separated from each other (recall that the authors used the same C_D for all experiments). 

C_M controls alpha_w in the inertia limit

d did not have any effect

C_f has the most marked effect. Especially since the plant parameters dont change. Remeber that in the unidirectional limit, the ratio alpha reduces to sqrt(Ld/Ls)

If you want the curves to look exactly like those obtained by Lowe et al (2005), you need to use their plant values (changing S and d) and the varying C_f. 

CONTENTS of the .MAT file(s)
d -> depth
H -> Wave Height
h_c -> canopy height
S -> stem separation
t_v -> plant thickness
TS -> (structure) Time Series 
	Sd_ratio = S/d
	b_v -> plant width
	C_f -> friction coefficient
	alpha -> flow attenuation parameter
	A_S_ratio -> time series of A/S 
U -> generic Velocity Time Series
z -> height of alpha calculation
resources.name: Time Series of Flow Attenuation Parameter (alpha)

resources.description:
Data supporting Figure 9 in Villanueva et al. 2023

variables are disambiguated and compared to each other. Param_Table (DATA) is used as base and the data extracted in different tables shown here, where the variable name indicates the variables and positions compared. 
d -> depth, with values being 1,2, and 3 corresponding to depth 1,2 and 3 as described in the paper. 
H -> Wave Height, with values showing ranges in cm after "H"
T -Y Wave Period, with values showing the period in seconds after "T"

suffixes (after the underscore) correspond to the alpha ratio calculation positions, e.g. 14 means that the velocity at position 4 was divided by that at position 1, thus obtaining the flow attenuation between positions 1 and 4, or alpha_w,1-4 in the figure.

resources.description:
Data for Figure 8 in Villanueva et al. 2023

Full_Table (168 runs) Data for the velocities (see variable names of Param_Table.mat)

Data is also separated and averaged for all runs, disambiguated by the ADV position (i.e. z-coordinate). Mean values for all measurements shown in D_zAVG_all and the error in D_zAVG_e_all. The Structures with no "_all" correspond to the values for each mat configuration.
resources.name: Velocities at each height and averaged values

resources.description:
These tables contain the processed averaged data for the trials with ASG (X1) used for Villanueva et al. 2022 and to initiate calculations of Villanueva et al. 2023

I post-processed the data and calculated the average values of all repetitions belonging to one T-H combination (run). The velocities (u and w) correspond to the reading of the ADVs at the bottom (i.e. 3.3 cm from the bed, code: A1). For the rest of the devices, the values at all heights (A1-A5) were averaged and the error calculated. NOTE: For the plots, it is necessary to substract the control values in order to identify the real forces caused by the mats with ASG.
resources.name: Bottom Average Data (Near Bead)
